lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: Stop! Don't step on the — oh. You didn't. Good.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: Those are carrots. Probably. I planted them yesterday and I've been checking.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: ...Are those real ears? Can I — no. Sorry. Grandma says you don't ask to touch people's ears.

lines.speaker: char_freyja
lines.text: They're real. They can also hear you whispering about them from the road.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: How old are you?

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: That's not a number. That's what Grandma says when she doesn't want to tell me either.

lines.speaker: char_freyja
lines.text: Your grandmother sounds sensible.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: A thousand? That's more than all my fingers and toes. Times... a lot of times.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: I'm writing it down. I have a book of facts. You're fact forty-one.

lines.speaker: char_freyja
lines.text: What was fact forty?

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: Goats can't eat tin. Grandma's goat didn't know that either.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: Ten and three-quarters. Now you go. That's the rule.

lines.speaker: char_freyja
lines.text: A thousand and some. I stopped counting the quarters.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: ...You stopped counting a whole thousand?

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: I'm Pippa. I'm staying with Grandma Edda for spring, because Mum says Grandma's getting stubborn.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: I think she was always stubborn and now there's just more time for it.

lines.speaker: char_freyja
lines.text: Freyja. I'm a mage. Mostly I'm passing through.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: A MAGE? A real one? Can you do lightning? Can you make Grandpa's garden come back?

lines.speaker: char_freyja
lines.text: Your grandfather's garden?

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: Behind the house. Grandpa Jonas planted it. Grandma says it was flowers all the way to the trees.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: Now it's just grass. Grandma's knees don't bend anymore, and I tried, but I think I planted the seeds upside down.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: She's inside. She'll pretend she doesn't want company. She does.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: Grandma's inside. Knock loud. She says she can't hear, but she can.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: Are you really doing it? The garden? Can I watch? I won't talk. Much.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: It's round the back. Where the grass looks bored.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: You DID it! There's a blue one! There's a — what's that one?

lines.speaker: char_freyja
lines.text: Sky bell. Or harebell, around here. Or 'the blue one.'

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: I'm writing 'the blue one.'

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: Will they stay? Forever?

choices.text: Until autumn. Then seeds. Then spring again.
As long as someone looks after them.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: That's not forever.

lines.speaker: char_freyja
lines.text: Nothing is. Flowers just admit it sooner.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: ...I'm writing that down too. Grandma's on the bench. Go! She's doing her not-crying face.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: Then I'll look after them. I'm here till summer. And next spring. Probably.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: Grandma's on the bench. Go! She's doing her not-crying face.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: I counted {flowers_counted} flowers before I lost count. Then I started again and got a different number.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: I wrote down what you said. About forever. Grandma read it and went quiet and then made me a pancake.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: I'm in charge of watering now. Grandma says not the bluebells, they like it dry. I'm writing that down.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: When you come back I'll be taller. You'll be the same, I bet. That's fact forty-two.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: Oh! And. There's another thing. You know the oak by the bench?

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: Grandpa's stone is under it. It's got moss all over. Grandma used to scrub it every Sunday, and then her knees stopped, and then she just sort of stopped too.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: I tried to read it once. It says JON and then moss and then something about a hat. I think. I wasn't sure about the hat.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: The same flowers? The blue ones?

lines.speaker: char_freyja
lines.text: If the spell allows it. It tends to have opinions.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: It's up past the bench, under the oak. Don't tell Grandma I told you. She'll know I told you.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: Okay. It's not going anywhere. That's sort of the point of stones.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: It's up past the bench, under the oak. I'll stay here and not watch.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: ...I'm going to watch a bit.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: I SAW! From the meadow! There's blue on Grandpa!

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: Go and tell Grandma. She's pretending she didn't see.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: Did you read it? Great-Grandma's book? I tried once. It's mostly sums.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: And one page about getting jam out of a tablecloth, in a rhyme. It smells like her kitchen. I don't know how a book remembers a kitchen.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: Does the stain one work on other things?

lines.speaker: char_freyja
lines.text: Most things. Within reason. And moss, apparently.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: Then can you do the statue? By the road, where you came in. Everyone walks past it. Even Grandma, and she says hello to the signpost.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: It's got a face but the moss ate most of it. I say good morning to it anyway. In case.

lines.speaker: char_freyja
lines.text: In case of what?

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: In case it's someone.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: You say good morning first. That's the rule. It's polite.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: South, by the road. Where you came in. Say good morning first.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: You've got your thinking face. The one for when something's older than you. Which is hardly ever. What did it say?

choices.text: It says my name. It's a statue of me.
I don't remember doing it. They did.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: YOU? You have a STATUE?

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: Does it have the ears?

lines.speaker: char_freyja
lines.text: It has a hat I've never owned.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: That's fact forty-three. 'The elf has a statue and it's wearing the wrong hat.'

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: I'm going to say good morning to it properly now. Knowing.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: You don't remember? But they did. Whoever it was put it there, and everyone just walked past it for years.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: And I said good morning every day. And it was you.

lines.speaker: char_freyja
lines.text: Then you were being polite to the right person all along.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: That's fact forty-three. I'm underlining it.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: I told Grandma the statue is you. She said 'I could have told you that,' and then she said she couldn't have, and then she went to look.

lines.speaker: char_pippa
lines.text: It's a rule now, in the book. You say good morning to people even if you don't know who they are. Especially.
